correctness.rationale: For the explicitly stationary Gaussian diffusion, the cross-time covariance equals a damped planar rotation, and noisy sampling adds a diagonal covariance term. Circular polarization diagonalizes the spectral matrices, and geometric-decay Toeplitz-to-circulant comparison reduces full-path relative entropy to a positive scalar frequency integral. Exact Poisson-kernel convolution gives the closed formula. Its Puiseux expansion gives the displayed fixed-noise square-root coefficient. Strictly positive Gaussian covariance at zero spacing for each fixed observation block yields a quadratic finite-block KL, proving the noncommuting iterated limits. The independent standard-library numerical verifier passed 36 deterministic cross-checks. These checks are corroboration, not a substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Exact noisy-trajectory entropy-production recovery resolves a nontrivial ambiguity identified by Gingrich et al.: shorter windows can falsely suggest diminished irreversibility when measured more often. The universal-in-history noncommutation and explicit nonanalytic coefficient provide a sharp diagnostic in a physically motivated, minimal rotational Gaussian model. They distinguish full-path inference from a fixed-order proxy without asserting general results for arbitrary hidden stochastic systems.
